attribution.note: Marcus directly asserts the losses, pricing changes and customer resistance.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves all three present-tense observations and the illustrative providers.

contract.note: Recent quarterly net losses, effective price increases and observable complaints are reasonable ordinary measures. The contract appropriately avoids requiring every provider to exhibit every component.

evidence.note: Dated reporting establishes higher effective costs and customer opposition at Anthropic. It does not establish financial losses or the complete provider pattern.

Reports substantial OpenAI Q1 net losses for the selected period and was published before evaluation. This supports the loss component despite later publication than the statement; underlying private records remain unavailable.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI losses and Anthropic pricing resistance have supporting evidence. Comparable losses and the broader commercial pattern among the named providers remain insufficiently established. Missing coverage is not contrary evidence.

attribution.note: Marcus makes this assertion in his own voice.

semantics.note: The surrounding discussion identifies the material as AI-generated; the normalization preserves the institutional scope.

contract.note: A substantial recurring influx causing review burdens is a fair reading of inundation. Distinguishing supplier rejections from material reaching libraries preserves the named institutional scope.

evidence.note: The contemporaneous community record documents increasing improper AI use and burdensome cleanup. It supports the Wikipedia component, though it is qualitative moderation evidence rather than a quantitative measurement.

Hoopla discloses substantial supplier screening, combining AI-generated and other low-quality titles. Its statement that rejected titles never reached libraries limits the inference; it does not establish negligible influx across libraries.

reviews.rationale: Wikipedia's cleanup burden is supported. Library inundation remains unestablished because the supplier's combined rejection count neither isolates low-quality AI material nor measures library exposure. The screening disclosure also does not refute the broader claim.

attribution.note: Marcus endorses the causal assertion and explicitly expresses uncertainty about quality and sales.

semantics.note: The firm assertion concerns AI causing increased supply. The normalization retains uncertainty about quality and sales without turning it into categorical negative claims.

contract.note: The supply interpretation and distinction between average quality and expanded choice are reasonable. Quality and sales uncertainty must remain qualifications, not separately scored predictions or assertions of no benefit.

evidence.note: The dated research summary supports a large e-book supply increase associated with LLM adoption and lower average quality by its proxy. Better titles at some ranks and modeled choice benefits qualify this support. The supplied methods do not isolate AI's causal contribution.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes a substantial Amazon e-book increase and widespread author AI use, but does not adequately distinguish causal attribution from timing and association. Expanded-choice benefits do not contradict uncertainty about average quality or aggregate sales. Those hedged clauses receive no separate outcome grade.

attribution.note: The broad loss assertion is Marcus's own; it does not depend on attributing the nearby analyst quotation to him.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves multiple AI business layers and the special emphasis on agentic coding.

contract.note: Recent company-wide net losses are a reasonable ordinary reading. Requiring evidence across layers and a connection to coding preserves the assertion. An unspecified accounting basis does not automatically preclude assessment.

evidence.note: The filing discloses substantial Anthropic Q1 losses and was available before evaluation. Company-wide GAAP losses support the provider component, while fair-value charges and the absence of coding allocation limit further inference.

CoreWeave's disclosure establishes a substantial Q1 net loss at the infrastructure layer. Positive adjusted EBITDA or adjusted operating income uses different measures and does not negate that net loss.
The reported Cursor loss covers a different fiscal period and lacks a specified loss measure. It is relevant background but does not fit the contract's comparable Q1 net-loss requirement.

reviews.rationale: Disclosures support large Q1 losses at model-provider and infrastructure layers. The packet lacks comparable coding-application results and evidence establishing the special concentration in agentic coding. Partial support without contrary findings does not settle the full claim.
